query_text: Create a language formality tone checker app for my phone where I can paste in a message and it tells me how formal or casual it sounds, something like a little meter from super formal to very chill, and maybe highlights the words or phrases that are pushing it one way or the other so I know what to tweak before I send it.

Make a mobile app that acts like a vocabulary guide for switching between different ways of talking, so if I need to say the same thing in a casual way versus a professional way I can just tap a situation and see word swaps, like it shows you the stuffy version next to the relaxed version so you can pick what fits the moment.

Make a mobile app that gives me ready-to-use phrase cards for getting out of social situations gracefully, like a set of exit lines organized by how awkward the situation is, from just needing a polite wrap-up to a full emergency escape, so I can glance at my phone and pick something that sounds natural instead of panicking.

Need a mobile friendship tracker app where I can log each friend, rate how close we are right now, and get little reminders when I haven't reached out in a while, so the app kind of nudges me to check in before a friendship quietly fades without me noticing, with a simple list showing who needs some attention soon.

Make a group poll app for my phone where I can type in a bunch of activity ideas, send a link to my friends, and everyone taps their favorites so we can actually agree on what to do instead of going back and forth in the group chat forever, and it shows the results as a simple ranked list once people have voted.

Create a daily check-in reminder app for my phone that helps me and an accountability partner stay on track together, where each morning it gives us a simple prompt to answer about what we plan to do that day and we can see each other's answers, so we actually follow through instead of just saying we will.

Need a phrase bank app on my phone full of conversation starters and topic bridges I can pull up whenever a chat hits a dead stop, organized by situation like a one-on-one hangout versus a group thing versus a work lunch, so I can just glance at a few options and pick something that gets the conversation going again.

Build a daily compliment reminder app for my phone that nudges me once a day to give someone a genuine compliment, maybe suggests a few ideas so I'm not stuck thinking of something, and lets me log who I complimented each day so I can build up a streak and actually turn it into a real habit over time.

Make a mobile app that generates icebreaker questions for events or parties, where I can pick a vibe like fun and silly versus thought-provoking, and it gives me a handful of questions to use, so when I'm hosting something or walking into a networking thing I always have a good opener ready right on my phone.

Build a mobile app with conversation prompt cards for people who get anxious in social situations, where you tap a card and it shows you a simple way to start or continue a conversation, organized by setting like meeting new people versus hanging with acquaintances, so you always have something in your pocket to fall back on when your mind goes blank.

A pre-order countdown app for book or album releases where the whole screen feels like the cover art is breathing, with a big gorgeous timer showing days and hours until the drop date, and a soft animated background that matches the mood of the release so when I open it on my phone it feels like I'm already part of the moment.

Build a subscription renewal countdown app for my phone that shows all my recurring services in a clean list with a little timer next to each one counting down to the renewal date, so the design feels calm and organized, using soft colors and clear typography so I actually enjoy checking it instead of dreading the surprise charges.

Create a friendship anniversary reminder app for my phone that feels warm and personal, like a little card for each friend with their name, the date we met or became close, a small countdown to the next anniversary, and maybe a gentle color palette that feels nostalgic and cozy so opening it actually makes me smile and want to reach out.

A mobile countdown app for solar eclipses and other sky events where the main screen looks like a deep space view, with a glowing timer counting down to the next big astronomical event, and each event gets its own mood, a solar eclipse feeling dramatic and golden while a meteor shower feels more ethereal and dark-sky calm.

Make a 100-day personal resolution tracker for my phone that has a satisfying visual feel, like a grid of 100 little tiles you fill in one by one each day, with a warm color gradient that slowly builds as you get further into your streak so the whole thing looks beautiful half-filled and feels really rewarding to check each evening.

Build a moving-in countdown app for my phone that feels fresh and exciting to open, with a big timer showing how many days until move-in day and a simple checklist below it for all the tasks I need to knock out before then, using a clean airy look so the whole thing feels organized and like a fun adventure I'm preparing for.

Build a parenting milestone birthday countdown app for my phone that tracks each kid's next big birthday, like turning one or five or ten, with a warm illustrated feel, showing a countdown in days and a little note about what milestone that age represents so every time I open it on my phone it feels like celebrating something precious.

A weight-loss goal date tracker for my phone where I set a target date and my goal weight, and the app shows a gentle progress visual each time I log in, something motivating and soft-toned rather than clinical, with a countdown to the target date and a small encouraging note so it feels supportive and keeps me looking forward.

A 21-day habit countdown app for my phone where each day feels like a small ceremony, with a beautifully minimal screen showing the habit name, which day you're on, and a ring or progress arc that fills up over the 21 days in a satisfying slow color shift, so the whole thing looks like something you'd want to screenshot and share when you finish.

Create a baby due date countdown app for my phone that has a soft dreamy feel, showing a big gentle timer in weeks and days until the due date, with a pastel palette and a little illustrated detail that changes as the due date gets closer, so opening it feels comforting and celebratory during the whole waiting period.

Build a final exam countdown app for my phone that has a focused but encouraging feel, where I can add each exam with its date and subject, and the app shows a clean urgency timer for the soonest one with a study hours tracker below it, using a crisp high-contrast look that feels sharp and serious so it actually keeps me in the zone.

A color converter tool app on my phone where I can type or paste in a hex code and it instantly shows me the RGB, HSL, and CMYK values all at once, with a big color swatch so I can actually see what the color looks like, and a one-tap copy button next to each value so I stop wasting time switching between tabs to do this manually.

Make a Morse code app for my phone that lets me type regular text and see it converted to dots and dashes instantly, and also paste in Morse code to decode it back to plain text, with a clear two-way layout so I can use it quickly without figuring out which direction to go, great for games or just satisfying my curiosity about how it works.

Build a barcode label text generator app for my phone where I type in a name, price, or any short info and it spits out a ready barcode with the text underneath, so I can use it for labeling stuff around the house or small shop items, with a clean output I can screenshot and print rather than hunting for some complicated desktop tool every single time.

A text scrambler tool for my phone where I can type a message and pick either ROT13 or a simple cipher to encode it, and paste scrambled text back in to decode it, so my friends and I can send little coded notes for fun, with two clear input areas so the whole encode-decode flow is obvious and I'm not guessing which box does what.
